In order to facilitate public participation at meetings the City will accept public comment
in the following manner:

1. Whether participating in-person or virtually at the meeting, members of the public
  may provide public comment by submitting a speaker card prior to the start of public
  comment on that item, at the following webpage:

  www.cityofpasadena.net/commissions/public-comment/

  If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda item,
  please indicate which items on the online form (multiple item speakers will be
  handled according to the process posted on the agenda and as specified in the City
  meeting policy). Public comments are limited to 3 minutes each, and the Chair and
  Committee may limit this time if reasonable under the circumstances.

2. In-person Meeting Participation: Complete an online speaker card at the following
  website: www.cityofpasadena.net/commissions/public-comment/

  After submitting a public speaker card, members of the public may attend the
  meeting in-person by coming to the Pasadena City Council Chamber, Room S249
  at City Hall at the date and start-time of the posted meeting.

  Virtual Meeting Participation: For virtual participants, you may attend by
  connecting to the meeting using a computer, other electronic device, or by
  telephone. Please review the agenda to identify the published start time for the
  meeting and connect to the meeting just prior to, or at the start of the meeting.

  To participate in public comment for an item and to be recognized to speak, it is
  required that the speaker login to the meeting using the same name or telephone
  number used on the Speaker Card form. This will allow City staff to locate and
  promote the speaker into the meeting when it is time for their public comment.
  Participants’ phone calls to the Committee meeting will be recorded as part of the
  Committee meeting. By staying on the line and making public comment during the
   Committee meeting by phone, you are agreeing to have your phone call
  recorded. Following is the connectivity information for virtual participation:

  Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at: cityofpasadena.net/cczoom

  Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 161 482 446

3. Speaker Card Help Line: If a public comment speaker needs assistance in
  completing a speaker card, please call the City Clerk’s Office at: (626) 744-4124.
  Help line will open 30 minutes prior to the posted start time of the meeting.

4. Members of the public may submit correspondence of any length prior to the start of
  the meeting, at the following email address:

  gacevedo@cityofpasadena.net

  Correspondence will be forwarded to the Committee prior to the start of the meeting,
  posted online, and made part of the legislative record for the item.

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  April 29, 2024-6:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo and President Kenne called the Special Joint
  meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Unified School
  District (PUSD) Board of Education (Board) to order at 6:06 p.m.
  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by President Kenne.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Steve Madison
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams (arrived at 6:12 p.m.)

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  Chief Assistant City Attorney Javan Rad
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

Pasadena Unified School  President Kimberly Kenne
District, Board of Education  Vice President Jennifer Hall Lee
  Board Member Richardson Bailey
  Boardmember Patrick Cahalan
  Boardmember Patrice Marshall McKenzie
  Boardmember Dr. Yarma Velazquez
  Boardmember Tina Fredericks

  Staff:  Dr. Elizabeth J. Blanco, Ed.D., Superintendent of Schools
  Kingsley Udo, Chief Business Officer
  Dr. Helen Hill, Chief Academic Officer

  PRESENTATION FROM PASADENA UNIFIED SCHOOL
  DISTRICT ON SCHOOL SITE MAINTENANCE INCLUDING
  GARDENING LANDSCAPE INFORMATION

  Manuel Carrasco, PUSD Director of Facilities, provided a
  presentation on the recent facility enhancements at PUSD
  properties made throughout the school district, specifically
  relating to gardening and curb appeal, hie provided an oven/iew
  of the School District's efforts to maximize their current
  infrastructure and address the needs of maintenance of their
  facilities and landscaping.

Council Minutes  1  04/29/2024
   Councilmember Hampton expressed concerns that some
  parkways and curbsides appear to be overlooked in regard to
  proper maintenance, emphasizing areas of need near Cleveland
  Elementary and Washington Elementary.

  In response to President Kenne's concerns regarding the use of
  turf fields in the City, Councilmember Williams reported that the
  Senate Bill (SB 676) regarding turf fields will be discussed at a
  future Municipal Services Committee meeting, noting that the
  School District should participate in that discussion since
  PUSD's facilities and staff may be impacted.

  Councilmember Mlasuda thanked Director Carrasco, PUSD
  staff, and Amigos de los Rios, for their collaboration in
  beautifying the areas surrounding Willard Elementary.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 1 letter advocating for traffic
  improvements around Washington Elementary and La
  Pintoresca Library was received by the City Clerk's Office,
  distributed to the City Council and PUSD Board of Education,
  posted online, and made part of the public record for this item.

  The following individuals expressed concerns regarding the
  deferred maintenance at the Allendale Elementary campus and
  having Longfellow Elementary students temporarily utilize the
  campus under poorly maintained conditions:

  Paul Backstrom, Pasadena resident
  Beau Wammack, Pasadena resident

  Nina Chomsky, Linda Vista Annandale Association, spoke on
  the importance of maintaining closed school site properties to
  prevent degradation and impacts to adjacent neighborhoods.

  Rene Gonzalez, residence not stated, requested that a feature
  be created on the PUSD website to allow the public to take a
  photo and report maintenance issues.

  Councilmember Hampton suggested that since the City already
  has a Citizen Service Center (CSC) app, the public can report
  issues related to PUSD through the app so City staff can forward
  them to the School District, as an alternative to having the
  District develop an entirely new feature.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus of the Board of Education and City Council, the
  information was received and filed.

Council Minutes  2  04/29/2024
   UPDATE ON CAREER TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND
  APPRENTICESHIP PARTNERSHIPS

  Mayor Gordo introduced and thanked Congresswoman Judy
  Chu for securing federal funding to support career pathway
  opportunities for people of all ages within the Pasadena
  community.

  Congresswoman Chu announced that she was able to secure
  $1.8 million dollars in direct federal funding to support two of the
  City's project proposals - the Pasadena Facility for Jobs
  Creation, Training, and Education and the Pasadena Water
  Treatment Project. She reported that the funding will help cover
  labor, material, and construction costs for both projects.
  Phyllis Hallowell, Assistant to the City Manager, gave a
  presentation on the Career Technical Education Pilot program
  formalized through a partnership between Pasadena City
  College (PCC), PUSD, and the City of Pasadena. She reported
  that City staff will be touring a model Career Education Program
  in Kern County on Thursday, May 9, 2024.
  Dr. Helen Hill, Interim Chief Academic Officer, and Dr. Kristina
  Turley, College and Career Pathways Coordinator, presented
  the School District's High School Career Technical Education
  Pathways program and reported on student outcomes.
  Alton Wang, PCC College Board Chair, spoke on the importance
  of community partnerships to offer students with career
  development opportunities and pathways to long-term careers.
  Dr. Jose Gomez, PCC Superintendent, and Dr. Laura Ramirez,
  Vice President of Instruction, provided an update on the Career
  Technical Education programs offered by PCC. Dr. Ramirez
  reported on the various grants that PCC has received to fund a
  number of apprenticeship opportunities, and noted that PCC is
  working closely with PUSD to increase dual enrollment
  curriculum opportunities.

  The following individuals expressed concerns with the lack of
  allocated funding for special education and inclusivity of
  students with disabilities in the Career Education Technical
  programs offered by PCC.
  Rene Gonzalez, residence not stated
  Marlene Benites, Pasadena resident
  Zella Knight, Pasadena resident

Council Minutes  3  04/29/2024
   Superintendent Blanco reported that special education students
  are a part of Pathways program at John Muir High School and
  that PUSD has an agreement with PCC for PAL students
  between the ages 18 and 22 who attend classes.
  Councilmember Hampton advocated for students with
  disabilities to be actively included in discussions pertaining to
  career education.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.
  PRESENTATION REGARDING POTENTIAL AFFORDABLE
  HOUSING FOR PASADENA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT
  FACULTY AND STAFF, INCLUDING A DISCUSSION OF
  AB2295 AND SB35

  Kingsley Udo, PUSD Interim Chief Business Officer, provided
  introductory comments on the item, and PUSD Facilities Director
  Carrasco gave an overview of PUSD's efforts to identify
  affordable housing resources for faculty and staff. He stated that
  PUSD will be working closely with Education Housing Partners
  on preliminary due diligence, and reported that next steps
  include presenting options to the School Board for review,
  followed by submittal of an application to the City for approval.
  Jennifer Paige, Director of Planning, provided a presentation on
  Assembly Bill 2295 and Senate Bill 35, and responded to
  questions.

  Discussion ensued regarding income thresholds for the potential
  affordable housing units, the constraints on the use of proceeds,
  allowable land uses available to PUSD for use of its properties,
  and the Surplus Land Act.

  Mayor Gordo expressed concerns that repurposing school site
  properties that are not being used in a permanent manner would
  prevent such properties from returning to educational purposes.
  He noted that PUSD, the City, the Board of Education, and the
  City Council have a collective responsibility of ensuring the
  success of public education in Pasadena.
  Board Member Velasquez stated that the decline in student
  enrollment and local population reflects the need for community
  partnership, and emphasized the importance of supporting those
  who are disproportionately impacted in order to strengthen the
  K-12 system.

Council Minutes  4  04/29/2024
   In response to questions regarding options for use of affordable
  housing, Board Member Richardson Bailey expressed concerns
  that expanding the proposed project to include housing for
  members of the public that work in the community may create
  inconsistencies with the original intent of the housing project,
  which is to recruit and retain PUSD employees by providing
  affordable housing options.

  The following individuals expressed support and provided
  comments on the proposed affordable housing project for PUSD
  staff and faulty:

  Bert Newton, Making Housing and Community Happen
  Anthony Manousos, Pasadena resident
  Jill Shook, Pasadena resident
  Cindy Rice, Pasadena resident
  Carl Selkin, residence not stated
  Chase Stafford, Pasadena resident
  Rev. Marcos Canales, La Fuente Ministries Church
  Denise Robb, Throop Church

  The following individuals expressed opposition and/or concerns
  with the proposed affordable housing project for PUSD staff and
  faulty, and provided various comments and suggestions:
  Emily Stough, Altadena resident
  Rene Gonzalez, residence not stated
  Diane Kirby, Lower Hastings Ranch Association
  Jesse Dahlstrom, Pasadena resident
  Marlene Benites, Pasadena resident

  Caitlin Mahaffey, residence not stated, urged the City and
  School District to allow for flexibility as part of the proposed
  project, and urged for careful decision-making to ensure that
  immediate housing needs do not impact educational needs of
  students.

  Deirdre Duncan, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns
  pertaining to the availability of the affordable housing units in the
  City and urged for accountability.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 4 letters, in support of the
  affordable staff housing initiative at the Roosevelt site,
  supporting a second site for student family housing, and/or
  providing comments on this matter, were received by the City
  Clerk's office, distributed to the City Council and PUSD Board of
L..
  Education, posted online, and made part of the public record for
  this item.

  Council Minutes  5  04/29/2024
   Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus the Board of Education and City Council, the
  information was received and filed.

ADJOURNMENT  On the order of the President and Mayor, the special joint
  meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Board of Education
  adjour^ at 9:13 p.m.

  ^b
  Victor M. Gordo, Mayor
